title: Strings & Runes
description: Learn about string constants, runes, string manipulation, and formatting in Go
theory:
> **Curriculum:** This chapter follows [LEARN-LANGUAGES/CURRICULUM.md](../../CURRICULUM.md). Exercise ids are shared across LEARN-* repos for cross-reference.

## Strings

Immutable `str`, slicing, methods like `.startswith`, and f-strings for formatting.

exercises.title: String Constants
exercises.description: Declare a string variable greeting and assign it the value "Hello, Python!". Then print it using print.
hints: Use greeting := "Hello, Go!" to declare and assign

exercises.title: Using Runes
exercises.description: Declare a rune variable and assign it the Unicode character for 'A'. Print it using both %c and %d verbs to see character vs code point.
hints: Use fmt.Printf("Character: %c\n", ch) for the character
Use fmt.Printf("Code Point: %d\n", ch) for the Unicode code point

exercises.title: String Manipulation
exercises.description: Use strings.Contains to check if "Hello" is in "Hello, World!", strings.Replace to replace "World" with "Python", and strings.Split to split "a,b,c" by comma.
exercises.expected_output:
Contains: true
Replaced: Hello, Go!
First: a
exercises.solution:
text = "Hello, World!"
print("Contains:", str("Hello" in text).lower())
print("Replaced:", text.replace("World", "Go", 1))
print("First:", "a,b,c".split(",")[0])

exercises.title: String Formatting
exercises.description: Use fmt.Sprintf to format a string with a name and age, then print it. Also use printf to format a floating point number to 2 decimal places.
exercises.expected_output:
Alice is 30 years old
Pi is 3.14
hints: fmt.Sprintf("%s is %d years old", name, age) creates the formatted string
Use fmt.Printf("Pi is %.2f\n", pi) for 2 decimal places
exercises.solution:
name, age, pi = "Alice", 30, 3.14159
print(f"{name} is {age} years old")
print(f"Pi is {pi:.2f}")

exercises.title: To Upper and To Lower
exercises.description: Given s := "Python Programming", print it in all uppercase and then all lowercase.

exercises.title: Reverse a String
exercises.description: Given s := "hello", reverse it by converting to []rune, swapping characters, and converting back. Print the reversed string.
hints: Swap runes[0] with runes[len-1], runes[1] with len-2, etc.

exercises.title: String HasPrefix and HasSuffix
exercises.description: Declare url := "https://example.com". Check if it starts with "https://" and ends with ".com". Print both results.
